edit.description: The banner wording has one home — `pub const BANNER` (:31) — and this module's own test module spells a second: `const NOTE_BANNER` (:111) is byte-identical to it (verified by comparing the two literals this tick), declared inside `mod tests` whose `use super::*` already has `BANNER` in scope. Two consequences, both live: a `BANNER` re-wording leaves `placement_lines_round_trips_the_body_banner_of_a_frontmatterless_source` (:114) green over the retired text, asserting a round-trip of bytes the writer no longer emits; and the name misreports the subject, since `NOTE_*` is this module's prefix for the frontmatter note (`NOTE_MARKER`, `NOTE_COMMENT`) while the copy is the frontmatterless banner. Delete the copy and drive the test off `BANNER`, the constant `emit` places — the round-trip then pins the writer's own wording. The sibling test one function down already models the shape: it reads `NOTE_COMMENT` directly and then asserts `NOTE_COMMENT.starts_with(NOTE_MARKER)`, so the banner test can assert `BANNER.starts_with(BANNER_MARKER)` beside it for the same reason.

summary: placement.rs's banner round-trip test asserts over a hand copy of BANNER, so a re-wording leaves it green over text the writer no longer emits.

tests.asserts: the frontmatterless round-trip reads `BANNER` itself, and `BANNER.starts_with(BANNER_MARKER)` — so a re-worded banner that stops carrying its own marker fails rather than passing over a stale copy

acceptance: `cargo test` green with `const NOTE_BANNER` gone from `src/placement.rs` and the round-trip test reading `BANNER`.
notes: Posture sweep at src/install.rs, reached through its `crate::placement` import. Disjoint from the two guard-message folds filed this tick (different file) and from every other queued entry — no serialization needed. scoped at 2fc9bed3
